title: Investigate selective quantized kernel regression causing tail-latency spikes
creator: Arjun Patel
description: After a scheduler tweak that changed request routing heuristics (short-first preference), we observed intermittent tail-latency spikes and throughput drops for a subset of production workloads using quantized kernels. This ticket captures the investigation, RCA, mitigations applied, and follow-up action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-22: Alert from ops — elevated P99 latency for embeddings-serving cluster in us-west-2
2026-02-22 03:10 UTC: On-call verified correlated increase in compute-side CPU fallback logs and higher context-switches on GRU instances
2026-02-22 04:05 UTC: Temporary routing rollback to previous scheduler version (hotfix) reduced tail latency by ~45%
2026-02-23: Root cause analysis started — reproduced in staging with histogram-based trace and kernel guardrails enabled
2026-02-25: Hotfix PR (#4578) merged to add additional kernel selection guards and increased telemetry

rca_summary: The regression was caused by an interaction between a scheduler heuristic (which favored prioritizing short sequences to reduce average latency) and recently landed optimizations in the quantized kernel selection path. For certain long-context requests, the scheduler frequently interleaved them with short requests causing fragmented KV-cache patterns. The kernel selector misclassified a subset of model partitions as compatible with the new fused-quant kernels due to a stale capability matrix, triggering a runtime code path that performed a fallback to a CPU-based reference implementation for specific attention routines. The combination produced higher context-switching and cache churn, increasing P95/P99 latency and reducing throughput for affected tenants.
mitigations: Rolled back scheduler change to previous stable heuristic as a hotfix (temporary) — reverted on 2026-02-22
Added runtime guard: validate kernel capability matrix at load-time and reject mismatches to prevent silent selection of unsupported quantized kernels
Implemented a soft-fallback threshold: if CPU-fallback rate > 0.5% over 5 minutes, autoscale and route to fallback-compatible pool with capacity isolation
Improved telemetry: per-request kernel decision tags (kernel_variant, capability_version, fallback_reason) emitted to tracing and logs
Increased canary window and introduced sequence-length diversity in canary traffic
